title: EvidenceBatch
description: The payload a client uploads to POST /v1/sessions/{id}/batches. Student A produces this; Student C validates it. Source: Terrastep plan section 16 (API contracts) and section 17 (authoritative referee). The server NEVER accepts client-supplied points as truth - it recomputes capped contributions itself.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated, unique per batch, stable across retries. Plan section 16: the same batch resubmitted after a timeout must return the same canonical receipt. A repeated key with DIFFERENT content must return a conflict and be investigated.

session_id.description: The SERVER-issued session id from POST /v1/sessions, not the client's local UUID.

installation_id.description: Identifies this app install. Must match the device bound to the session ticket, or the batch is rejected.

sequence_end.description: Inclusive. Must be >= sequence_start. Gaps in the sequence are a rejection reason, not a warning - a gap means missing evidence.

rule_version.description: Must match the rule_version on the session ticket. A mismatch means the client is scoring under stale rules and the batch is rejected.

time_anchor.description: One trusted pair tying monotonic elapsed time to a UTC instant. Plan section 9: the phone's wall clock alone is insufficient to bound activity age. Everything else is derived from this anchor plus monotonic offsets.

samples.description: Bounded on purpose. Plan section 16 requires request-size limits. At 10s sampling a 60s batch carries ~6 location samples; 200 is generous headroom for motion events.

integrity.description: Play Integrity verdict, when available. Plan section 18: this is ONE signal among several. Attestation does not prove physical walking, and its absence must never by itself ban anyone.

sequence.description: Must fall within [sequence_start, sequence_end] and be strictly increasing across the array.

elapsed_ms.description: Monotonic. Must be non-decreasing across the array. The server rejects non-monotonic sequences rather than silently reordering them.
